MASTER PROJECT TASK: CONVERT TIKTOK LIVE TEMPLE RPC INTO GENERAL CHRISTIAN PRAYER LIVE (US MARKET)

You are an autonomous senior full-stack developer working on an existing project.

GitHub source: https://github.com/zane-tv/tiktok-live-temple-rpc

PROJECT LOCATION: Existing local repository: tiktok-live-temple-rpc-main

OBJECTIVE:

Transform the existing Vietnamese Buddhist TikTok livestream application into a professional GENERAL CHRISTIAN PRAYER LIVE platform targeting viewers in the United States.

The new project brand:

CHRISTIAN PRAYER LIVE

Main tagline:

FAITH • HOPE • LOVE

Secondary tagline:

"Pray Together. Grow in Faith."

IMPORTANT:

Work directly in the existing source code.
Do not rebuild the application from scratch.
Preserve all working infrastructure.
Do not delete existing functionality unnecessarily.
Do not break the current Windows installation.
Make changes incrementally.
Back up files before modifying important modules.
Test actual functionality instead of only changing text and CSS.
================================================== PHASE 1: ANALYZE THE EXISTING PROJECT

Before editing, inspect the entire repository.

Read and understand:

package.json
server.js
tts_worker.py
public/
public/js/
public/css/
config/
config/piper/en/
config/piper/vn/
data/
all existing RPC modules
all TikTok event handlers
OBS browser source
admin dashboard
existing TTS implementation

Identify:

How TikTok Live connects.
How comments are received.
How likes, follows, shares and gifts are handled.
How JSON-RPC works.
How WebSocket communicates.
How OBS renders the livestream.
How TTS is queued and played.
How backgrounds and visual effects are loaded.

Create a short implementation plan before modifying files.

Do not make assumptions about existing file names or APIs.

================================================== PHASE 2: PRESERVE EXISTING INFRASTRUCTURE

Keep all existing working functionality:

Bun.js server.
TikTok Live Connector.
TikTok username/room connection.
TikTok comment listener.
Like listener.
Follow listener.
Share listener.
Gift listener.
JSON-RPC 2.0.
WebSocket.
OBS browser source.
1080x1920 vertical livestream.
Admin dashboard.
TTS queue.
Audio playback.
Python environment.
Piper voice models.
ZeroTTS fallback.
Existing RPC methods.

Do not rename or remove RPC endpoints.

Do not modify API structures unless necessary.

Do not break compatibility with existing OBS scenes.

================================================== PHASE 3: GENERAL CHRISTIAN BRANDING

Replace the Buddhist temple identity with:

CHRISTIAN PRAYER LIVE

Target market: United States.

Religious direction: GENERAL CHRISTIAN.

The content must be welcoming to viewers from different Christian traditions.

Do not focus exclusively on Catholicism or Protestantism.

Use broadly recognizable Christian themes:

Jesus Christ.
Christian faith.
Prayer.
Hope.
Love.
Forgiveness.
Gratitude.
God's grace.
Bible-inspired encouragement.
Peace.
Spiritual reflection.

Remove Buddhist-specific content from the user-facing interface:

Buddha.
Buddhist temples.
Lotus offerings.
Buddhist rituals.
Buddhist fortune telling.
Buddhist merit systems.
Buddhist prayers.
Buddhist symbols.

Do not delete old source files if they are still required for compatibility. Replace the user-facing experience.

All user-facing content must use natural American English.

================================================== PHASE 4: PROFESSIONAL LIVESTREAM DESIGN

Create a premium Christian livestream visual experience.

Brand:

CHRISTIAN PRAYER LIVE

Tagline:

FAITH • HOPE • LOVE

Secondary text:

"Pray Together. Grow in Faith."

Visual direction:

Beautiful Christian church interiors.
Illuminated crosses.
Holy Bible.
Church stained glass.
Prayer candles.
Sunrise.
Golden light rays.
Peaceful skies.
Elegant Christian artwork.
Soft floating particles.
Cinematic lighting.

Color palette:

Deep navy.
Warm gold.
Ivory white.
Soft beige.
Dark charcoal.

Avoid excessive animations.

The design should look professional, peaceful and trustworthy.

OBS layout:

1080x1920.
Vertical 9:16.
Mobile-readable text.
Responsive layout.
Clear prayer request area.
Live comments.
Community activity.
Attractive event notifications.

Create an attractive central Christian visual with a cross as a primary symbol.

================================================== PHASE 5: AUTOMATIC IMAGE DISCOVERY AND DOWNLOAD

VERY IMPORTANT:

Do not use only placeholder images.

Find, download and integrate real Christian-themed image assets.

Use reputable image sources:

Unsplash.
Pexels.
Pixabay.
Wikimedia Commons.

Only use images with suitable licenses for commercial livestream broadcasting.

Check license and attribution requirements.

Do not download random copyrighted images.

IMAGE CATEGORIES:

Christian cross.
Church interior.
Stained glass.
Holy Bible.
Prayer candles.
Jesus Christ artwork.
Sunrise and peaceful skies.
Christian worship atmosphere.
Golden light backgrounds.
Peaceful landscapes.

Create this asset structure:

public/assets/christian/

backgrounds/ cross/ church/ bible/ candles/ jesus/ overlays/

Download approximately 10-20 high-quality images if suitable assets are available.

Requirements:

Prefer high-resolution images.
Prefer vertical images or images suitable for 9:16 cropping.
Optimize image sizes.
Use descriptive filenames.
Avoid duplicate images.
Verify downloaded files.
Record original source URLs.
Record license information.
Record attribution requirements.

Create:

public/assets/christian/asset-manifest.json

The manifest should include:

Filename.
Category.
Source.
License.
Attribution.
Image dimensions if available.

Do not claim an image was downloaded unless the file actually exists.

Do not use remote image URLs during the livestream.

All downloaded assets must be served locally.

If image downloading is unavailable, create the folder structure and report which images still need to be added.

================================================== PHASE 6: AUTOMATIC BACKGROUND ROTATION

Implement automatic background rotation for OBS.

Example rotation:

Beautiful church interior.
Cross at sunrise.
Holy Bible with candlelight.
Peaceful Christian landscape.
Church stained glass.
Christian prayer candles.
Golden illuminated cross.

Requirements:

Smooth fade transitions.
Configurable interval.
No abrupt flashing.
No distracting effects.
Keep prayer text readable.
Use dark overlays when necessary.
Avoid loading external URLs.

Admin controls:

Enable/disable background rotation.
Select background category.
Change background manually.
Set rotation interval.
Preview available backgrounds.
Randomize backgrounds.

Use locally downloaded images.

================================================== PHASE 7: TIKTOK INTERACTION SYSTEM

Preserve existing TikTok event structures.

Adapt existing events to Christian interactions.

LIKE:

Display subtle golden light particles around the cross.

FOLLOW:

Display:

"Welcome to our prayer community. God bless you!"

SHARE:

Display:

"Thank you for sharing faith, hope and love!"

COMMENT COMMANDS:

AMEN: Display a beautiful AMEN animation.

PRAY: Display:

"Let us pray together."

JESUS: Display a Jesus-centered inspirational message.

FAITH: Display an inspirational faith message.

HOPE: Display a message about hope.

LOVE: Display a message about God's love.

PRAYER: Invite viewers to submit prayer requests.

GOD: Display a short inspirational Christian message.

THANK YOU: Display a gratitude animation.

Avoid repeating the same messages too frequently.

Add configurable message templates.

Use the existing TikTok event payloads.

Do not invent event fields.

================================================== PHASE 8: PRAYER REQUEST SYSTEM

Implement an interactive prayer request system.

Accept comments such as:

PRAY FOR ME PRAYER REQUEST PLEASE PRAY PRAY FOR MY FAMILY

When detected:

Add the request to a prayer queue.
Display a visually attractive prayer notification.
Show the viewer's TikTok display name when available.
Keep messages concise.
Avoid displaying sensitive personal information.
Prevent spam.
Add configurable moderation.

Example:

"Sarah is asking for prayers for her family."

Community message:

"Let us keep Sarah and her family in our prayers."

Add a prayer request queue to the admin dashboard.

Admin controls:

Approve request.
Hide request.
Remove request.
Pause prayer notifications.
Clear queue.

Do not make promises of guaranteed healing, wealth, miracles or supernatural outcomes.

Never require viewers to send gifts to receive prayers.

================================================== PHASE 9: TIKTOK GIFTS

Adapt existing gift handlers.

Use Christian-themed animations.

Small gifts:

Small prayer candle.
Soft golden light.
Thank-you notification.

Medium gifts:

Illuminated cross animation.
Beautiful candlelight effect.

Large gifts:

Special celebration.
Golden light rays.
Community gratitude message.

Example messages:

"Thank you for supporting our prayer community."

"May your kindness inspire hope and love."

Do not imply that gifts purchase blessings, prayers, healing or salvation.

Keep existing gift event processing and gift IDs.

================================================== PHASE 10: PIPER MULTILINGUAL TTS

VERY IMPORTANT:

The existing project contains:

config/piper/en/ config/piper/vn/

Inspect both directories recursively.

Identify actual installed voice files:

.onnx
.onnx.json

Read model metadata.

Do not assume model names.

Implement language-aware voice selection.

ENGLISH:

Default language: en-US.
Use an available American English Piper voice.
Natural American pronunciation.
Correct English punctuation.
Appropriate speaking speed.
Clear and friendly narration.

VIETNAMESE:

Default language: vi-VN.
Use the existing Vietnamese Piper voice.
Preserve Vietnamese pronunciation.

Requirements:

English messages must use English TTS.
Vietnamese messages must use Vietnamese TTS.
Do not send English through a Vietnamese-only text sanitizer.
Preserve the existing TTS queue.
Prevent overlapping speech.
Preserve existing audio playback.
Preserve OBS integration.
Add voice testing controls.
Add voice selection in admin dashboard.
Allow TTS to be disabled.
Allow language configuration.

Keep ZeroTTS as an optional fallback if already functional.

Do not delete or overwrite existing voice models.

Do not download voice models automatically.

Do not invent Piper CLI commands.

Inspect the installed Piper implementation before integrating or changing its invocation.

================================================== PHASE 11: ENGLISH PRAYER AND MESSAGE LIBRARY

Create a reusable English message library.

Categories:

Welcome messages.
Prayer invitations.
Faith encouragement.
Hope messages.
Love messages.
Gratitude messages.
Bible-inspired encouragement.
Community appreciation.
Gift thank-you messages.
Closing messages.

Use natural American English.

Messages should be short and suitable for live speech.

Avoid repetitive messages.

Avoid fabricated Bible quotations.

If quoting Scripture, verify the book, chapter and verse.

Store messages separately from application logic so they can be edited easily.

================================================== PHASE 12: ADMIN DASHBOARD

Convert the existing admin dashboard into English.

Preserve existing functionality.

Add or improve:

TikTok connection status.
Current live room information.
Live comments.
Like counter.
Follow counter.
Share counter.
Gift counter.
Prayer request queue.
Prayer message management.
Background selection.
Background rotation.
English voice selection.
Vietnamese voice selection.
TTS test button.
TTS enable/disable.
Voice status.
Speech volume.
Speech speed if supported.
Live event configuration.

Make the dashboard easy to use.

Do not remove existing RPC controls.

================================================== PHASE 13: CONFIGURATION

Use a configuration file or environment variables where appropriate.

Example settings:

DEFAULT_LANGUAGE=en DEFAULT_EN_VOICE=auto DEFAULT_VN_VOICE=auto

CHRISTIAN_THEME=true BACKGROUND_ROTATION=true BACKGROUND_ROTATION_INTERVAL=60

TTS_ENABLED=true

Use the actual discovered voice filenames.

Do not hardcode incorrect paths.

Preserve existing configuration.

================================================== PHASE 14: WINDOWS COMPATIBILITY

The application runs on Windows using:

XAMPP directory structure.
Bun.
Python 3.12.
uv.
Windows virtual environment.

Python executable:

.venv\Scripts\python.exe

Use Windows-compatible paths.

Do not assume:

bin/python python3

Use path.join() and pathlib.Path appropriately.

Do not break the existing working ZeroTTS local model configuration.

Do not modify the working model cache unnecessarily.

================================================== PHASE 15: TESTING

After modifications, run actual tests.

JavaScript:

Syntax checks.
Bun startup.
TikTok connector initialization.
RPC endpoint.
WebSocket endpoint.

Python:

Python syntax.
Piper voice discovery.
English voice initialization.
Vietnamese voice initialization.
English speech test.
Vietnamese speech test.

Frontend:

OBS browser source.
1080x1920 rendering.
Background rotation.
Prayer notifications.
Gift animations.
Admin dashboard.

TikTok:

Comment handling.
AMEN command.
PRAY command.
FAITH command.
Like handling.
Follow handling.
Share handling.
Gift handling.

Do not claim tests passed unless they were actually executed.

If TikTok credentials or an active LIVE session are unavailable, clearly report that those tests require a real session.

================================================== PHASE 16: FINAL REPORT

At completion, provide a detailed report:

Files modified.
Files created.
Features implemented.
Images downloaded.
Image source and license information.
Piper English model detected.
Piper Vietnamese model detected.
TTS architecture.
Tests actually passed.
Tests not performed.
Remaining issues.
Exact Windows startup commands.

Do not leave the project in a broken state.

If an implementation causes a regression, fix it before completing.

FINAL PRIORITY:

A stable, professional Christian Prayer Live application for the United States market, preserving the existing TikTok Live RPC architecture and working OBS integration.

Do not rebuild from scratch. Work directly in the existing repository.

# ✝ CHRISTIAN PRAYER LIVE

**FAITH • HOPE • LOVE**

> *"Pray Together. Grow in Faith."*

A peaceful, interactive **9:16 vertical livestream prayer room** for TikTok Live, built for viewers in the United States. The project keeps the original Bun.js + JSON-RPC 2.0 + WebSocket + OBS architecture and the working Windows/Piper installation, while replacing the Buddhist temple experience with a general Christian prayer community.

The room is intentionally **general Christian** — welcoming to viewers across traditions. It focuses on Jesus Christ, prayer, hope, love, forgiveness, gratitude, grace, Scripture-inspired encouragement and peace.

![Christian Prayer Live cathedral OBS stage](docs/screenshots/cathedral-stage-final.jpg)

---

## What is included

| Area | Implementation |
| --- | --- |
| Brand | Christian Prayer Live, deep navy / warm gold / ivory palette |
| Layout | 1080×1920 (9:16), auto-scaled for OBS browser source and desktop preview |
| Live connection | TikTok Live Connector: comments, likes, follows, shares, gifts |
| API | JSON-RPC 2.0 over HTTP (`/rpc`) and WebSocket (`/ws`) |
| Narration | Local Piper worker, American English + Vietnamese voices |
| Prayer requests | Moderated queue with approve / hide / remove / pause / clear |
| Backgrounds | 21 locally served licensed photographs + automatic fade rotation |
| Default scene | Licensed Gothic cathedral Mass with altar crucifix and praying congregation |
| Admin | English dashboard for connection, prayer queue, voices, backgrounds, messages |
| Compatibility | Original `temple.*` RPC methods and OBS URL preserved |

### Stage

- Full-frame cathedral scene: high Gothic arches, stained glass, altar crucifix and a gathered congregation.
- Warm golden grade, soft light aura, drifting particles and a gentle vignette.
- No floating hero cross and no baked-in text; the photograph itself is the main subject.
- Compact prayer request and “Verse of the Moment” cards above the lower panels.
- **Live Comments** and **Community Activity** in a single translucent bottom card.
- Counter strip for prayers, candles, amens, followers and gifts.
- Event overlays: AMEN, prayer invitation, gratitude, welcome and tiered gift celebrations.
- Optional quick-controls dock on desktop; `?obs=1` hides it for a clean broadcast.
- Small on-stream photo credit for CC BY / CC BY-SA backgrounds.

![Ministry dashboard](docs/screenshots/admin-dashboard.png)

# Cathedral Congregation Stage — Complete and Verified

The OBS stage now uses a full-frame, photorealistic cathedral scene as its main subject: high Gothic arches, stained glass, an altar crucifix, warm golden light, pews and a gathered congregation. The previous floating cross treatment is gone, and the photograph fills the entire 1080×1920 frame behind the existing HTML overlays. **No text, logos or captions are baked into the image.**

![Christian Prayer Live cathedral OBS stage](docs/screenshots/cathedral-stage-final.jpg)

## Final stage files

| File | Change |
| --- | --- |
| [server.js](server.js) | Registered the `cathedral` category, added both scenes to the background catalog, made `cathedral-01` the startup scene, and kept rotation/API behavior unchanged |
| [config/app.config.json](config/app.config.json) | Default rotation category is now `cathedral` |
| [public/index.html](public/index.html) | Removed the floating hero-cross markup so the photograph is the subject; retained the brand header, prayer card, verse, comments, activity, counters and footer overlays |
| [public/css/live.css](public/css/live.css) | Rebuilt the stage as a full-bleed photographic scene with the compact lower panel grid and reserved footer |
| [public/assets/christian/cathedral/cathedral-01-cathedral-mass.jpg](public/assets/christian/cathedral/cathedral-01-cathedral-mass.jpg) | Default scene, 1080×1920 |
| [public/assets/christian/cathedral/cathedral-02-sanctuary-service.jpg](public/assets/christian/cathedral/cathedral-02-sanctuary-service.jpg) | Alternate cathedral service, 1080×1920 |
| [asset-manifest.json](public/assets/christian/asset-manifest.json) | Source, license, author, dimensions and retrieval date for both scenes |
| [README.md](README.md) | Updated scene description, rotation defaults and test inventory |
| [scripts/smoke-test.js](scripts/smoke-test.js) | Background catalog assertion updated for the new category |

## Assets and licensing

- **Default:** *Cathedral Mass with Congregation* — Wikimedia Commons, **public domain**, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Centre-cropped to 9:16 and colour-graded; the source photograph contains no text and remains unaltered at its source URL.
- **Alternate:** *Sanctuary Service with Congregation* — Wikimedia Commons, **CC BY-SA 4.0**, Daniel G Rego. The stage shows a small on-stream credit automatically for CC-licensed scenes, and the admin shows the full credit.
- All backgrounds are served from `public/assets/christian/`; the frontend contains no remote image URLs.

## Verification actually performed

- **Stage:** opened `http://localhost:3000/?obs=1`, confirmed the stage element renders at a 9:16 ratio and the screenshot captured at exactly **1080×1920**.
- **Composition:** cathedral, altar crucifix, stained glass and congregation are clearly visible; the congregation occupies the middle and lower frame above the panels.
- **Overlays:** live comments, prayer card, verse, community list, counters and footer all render as separate HTML; no text is part of the image.
- **Rotation:** temporarily set the interval to 10 seconds in the `cathedral` category and observed the scene change from `cathedral-01` to `cathedral-02`; restored the broadcast default to **60 seconds**, random order, both scenes only.
- **Browser console:** no JavaScript errors on a fresh OBS-mode load.
- **API/WebSocket/TTS smoke suite:** **51/51 checks passed** after the redesign, including static assets, WebSocket notifications, backgrounds and both Piper languages.
- **Not tested:** a real TikTok LIVE session and OBS Studio playback itself — no live channel or OBS instance was available here.

The server is running with the new scene as the current background and rotation enabled. Open **http://localhost:3000/?obs=1** and add it to OBS at **1080×1920**.

The natural next step is to run one real LIVE session in OBS to confirm actual TikTok events align with the new bottom panel spacing on a broadcast encoder.

FEATURE: CHRISTIAN PRAYER LIVE – AMBIENT WORSHIP BACKGROUND MUSIC

Please add a professional background music system to the existing CHRISTIAN PRAYER LIVE application.

IMPORTANT: Modify the existing project in place. Do not rebuild the application.

1. MUSIC STYLE

Create a peaceful Christian prayer atmosphere suitable for US TikTok LIVE audiences.

Music characteristics:

Soft ambient Christian worship.
Gentle piano.
Warm atmospheric pads.
Subtle orchestral strings.
Gentle cinematic church ambience.
Peaceful, emotional and spiritual.
Slow tempo, approximately 55–75 BPM.
No vocals.
No lyrics.
No drums or strong percussion.
No sudden transitions or loud sounds.

The music should feel like a peaceful prayer session inside a beautiful cathedral.

Avoid dramatic movie trailers, energetic gospel, EDM and distracting melodies.

2. MUSIC SOURCE AND COPYRIGHT

Use original AI-generated instrumental music or properly licensed royalty-free music.

Do not download copyrighted commercial worship songs.

Do not imitate specific copyrighted songs or artists.

Store audio files locally in:

public/assets/christian/audio/

Create multiple original tracks:

peaceful-prayer-01
peaceful-prayer-02
cathedral-ambient-01
piano-worship-01
morning-prayer-01

Each track should be approximately 3–5 minutes and loop seamlessly.

If AI music generation is unavailable, use properly licensed royalty-free instrumental tracks.

Document all audio sources and licenses.

3. BACKGROUND MUSIC PLAYER

Implement a dedicated music player in the existing application.

Features:

Play / Pause.
Next track.
Previous track.
Volume slider.
Mute / Unmute.
Shuffle.
Repeat.
Automatic playlist rotation.
Remember selected track and volume.

Music must continue playing while TikTok comments and prayer requests update.

Do not restart music whenever the page receives a WebSocket event.

4. AUDIO MIXING

This is extremely important.

Background music must NEVER overpower the spoken prayer narration.

Default volume:

Background music: 8–12%.
Piper TTS narration: 85–100%.

Implement:

Smooth fade-in and fade-out.
Automatic music ducking when Piper speaks.
Restore music volume gradually after narration finishes.
Prevent clipping.
Avoid overlapping audio playback.

When Piper starts speaking, automatically reduce background music to approximately 3–5%.

When Piper finishes speaking, gradually restore the configured music volume.

5. ADMIN DASHBOARD

Add a new section:

BACKGROUND MUSIC

Controls:

Enable / Disable background music.
Play / Pause.
Select track.
Next / Previous.
Volume slider.
Auto-play toggle.
Shuffle toggle.
Repeat toggle.
Test audio.

Display:

Current track name.
Playback status.
Music volume.
Playlist.

The admin must allow me to change tracks without restarting the server.

6. OBS AND TIKTOK COMPATIBILITY

Preserve the existing OBS URL:

http://localhost:3000/?obs=1

Requirements:

Music must be audible through OBS Browser Source audio.
TikTok LIVE Studio must receive the music through the configured audio routing.
No music controls or player UI should appear on the clean OBS stage.
Music must not interfere with Piper TTS.
Do not create duplicate audio playback.
Handle browser autoplay restrictions properly.

Add an Enable Audio button if necessary.

7. STARTUP BEHAVIOR

When the application starts:

Load the playlist.
Do not autoplay before user interaction if the browser blocks autoplay.
Once audio is enabled, start the selected background track.
Keep music running continuously.
Recover gracefully if a track fails to load.
8. TESTING

Verify:

Music plays correctly.
Music loops without silence or abrupt cuts.
Piper narration ducks background music.
Music returns to normal volume after narration.
Changing tracks works.
Volume control works.
OBS receives the audio.
No duplicate playback.
No JavaScript errors.

Preserve all existing TikTok RPC, WebSocket, prayer queue, Piper TTS, background images and admin functionality.

At completion, provide a list of changed files, audio sources, licenses and test results.

FEATURE UPGRADE: CHRISTIAN PRAYER LIVE – INTERACTIVE LIVE SHOW

Upgrade the existing Christian Prayer Live application into an engaging, automated Christian prayer livestream for US TikTok audiences.

Do not rebuild the project. Preserve all existing functionality.

1. LIVE WELCOME SYSTEM

When a real TikTok viewer joins:

Welcome them by display name.
Show a beautiful welcome animation.
Generate a short English greeting using Piper TTS.
Avoid repeating greetings for the same viewer too frequently.

Example: "Welcome, Sarah! We're so glad you're here. May God's peace be with you today."

2. DAILY BIBLE VERSE

Create a rotating Bible verse system using verified KJV references.

Every 3–5 minutes:

Display a Bible verse.
Show its book, chapter and verse.
Add a short inspirational reflection.
Optionally narrate it using Piper TTS.

Avoid repeating recent verses.

3. AUTOMATED PRAYER PROGRAM

Create themed prayer sessions:

Morning Prayer.
Prayer for Healing.
Prayer for Family.
Prayer for Anxiety and Peace.
Prayer for Financial Difficulties.
Prayer for Strength.
Night Prayer.
Prayer of Gratitude.

Every 5–10 minutes, introduce a new prayer session.

Each prayer should be natural, compassionate, original English prose.

Do not promise miraculous outcomes or guaranteed healing.

4. REAL VIEWER INTERACTIONS

Handle actual TikTok events:

Viewer joins.
Comments.
AMEN.
PRAY.
Prayer requests.
Gifts.
Likes.
Shares.
Follows.

Each interaction should trigger an appropriate visual response.

Do not fabricate viewers, comments, gifts or engagement metrics.

5. PRAYER WALL

Build an attractive prayer request wall.

Features:

Display approved prayer requests.
Show first names or anonymous labels only.
Moderate inappropriate content.
Allow admin approval and removal.
Automatically rotate approved requests.
Piper can read approved prayers when enabled.
6. CONTINUOUS LIVE SHOW

Create a configurable programming schedule.

Example: 00:00 Welcome and peaceful introduction. 03:00 Bible verse. 06:00 Morning prayer. 10:00 Prayer for family. 15:00 Bible reflection. 20:00 Community prayer. 25:00 Prayer for healing. 30:00 Gratitude prayer.

Continue cycling without restarting the server.

Avoid overlapping Piper narration.

7. AUDIO EXPERIENCE
Continuous soft Christian ambient music.
Automatic volume ducking during narration.
Natural pauses between prayers.
No overlapping speech.
English US voice as default.
Configurable narration speed and volume.
8. ADMIN CONTROLS

Add:

Enable/disable automation.
Pause/resume program.
Select prayer theme.
Next prayer.
Next Bible verse.
TTS test.
Narration volume.
Music volume.
Welcome message toggle.
Prayer wall moderation.
Event history.

Allow manual control at all times.

9. IMPORTANT REQUIREMENTS
Use real TikTok events only.
Never simulate viewers or donations in production.
Do not repeatedly spam greetings.
Avoid repetitive prayers.
Respect viewer privacy.
Keep the visual presentation peaceful and professional.
Preserve the 1080x1920 OBS stage.
Preserve existing JSON-RPC and WebSocket compatibility.
10. TESTING

Test all features using clearly labeled simulated events.

Verify that real TikTok events are handled separately from test events.

Provide a report of modified files, actual tests and remaining limitations.

# Interactive Live Show — Built and Verified

Christian Prayer Live now runs an automated, narrated program on top of the existing TikTok/JSON-RPC pipeline. It cycles welcome, Scripture, prayer, community and gratitude segments, welcomes real viewers by name, rotates the prayer wall, and hands full manual control to the dashboard. The server is running at **http://localhost:3000/?obs=1** with the program live.

![Prayer cue on the OBS stage](docs/screenshots/live-show-stage-preview.jpg)

![Welcome cue on the OBS stage](docs/screenshots/live-show-welcome-preview.jpg)

## The program

| # | Segment | Holds | # | Segment | Holds |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Welcome & peaceful introduction | 2:00 | 7 | Bible verse | 2:30 |
| 2 | Bible verse | 2:30 | 8 | Prayer session | 3:30 |
| 3 | Prayer session | 3:00 | 9 | Bible reflection | 3:00 |
| 4 | Bible verse | 2:30 | 10 | Bible verse | 2:30 |
| 5 | Prayer session | 3:30 | 11 | Prayer of gratitude | 3:00 |
| 6 | Community prayer | 3:00 | 12 | Prayer session | 3:30 |

The cycle is ~35 minutes and repeats without a restart. Each cue fades a centered card onto the stage for 15–17 seconds, stays up while Piper is speaking, and is queued so prayers never talk over each other. Music ducks underneath.

- **Eight prayer themes** with three original prayers each: Morning, Healing, Family, Anxiety & Peace, Financial Hardship, Strength, Night, Gratitude. Recent themes and prayers are remembered, so wording does not repeat quickly. Nothing promises healing, wealth, miracles or salvation.
- **Twenty verified KJV verses** with an original short reflection each, stored in [messages.en.json](config/messages.en.json) so they remain editable. The last five references are avoided.
- **Welcomes** fire only from real TikTok `MEMBER` events, use the first name, and are rate-limited: once per viewer per 45 minutes, 20 seconds apart, max three per two minutes.
- **Prayer wall** rotates approved requests in the stage's right column, first names only. The community segment lifts one request up in prayer; the text is displayed, but narration uses only the first name so personal details are never read aloud.

![Live Show Automation panel](docs/screenshots/admin-live-show-panel.jpg)

## Admin controls

**Live Show Automation** panel: enable/disable, pause/resume, welcome toggle, program-narration toggle, prayer theme (rotate all or pin one), pace (Gentle 1.3× / Standard / Frequent 0.75×), **Next Segment**, **Next Bible Verse**, **Next Reflection**, **Next Prayer**, **Gratitude Prayer**, **Test Welcome**, **Restart Program**, live status, next-segment countdown and an auto/manual/test cue log. Compact equivalents sit in the stage's quick dock.

## Tests actually run

- **74/74 smoke checks passed**, including 12-segment schedule, 8 themes, 20 reflected KJV verses, labelled test welcome that doesn't count as a viewer, manual verse/prayer/reflection cues, pause/resume, configurable pace, and a `show.cue` WebSocket broadcast.
- **Real vs simulated separation:** simulated events carried a `simulated` flag, generated **no** welcome, and a simulated prayer request stayed off the prayer wall and out of the community cue. A red **DEMO MODE · SIMULATED ACTIVITY** badge appears on stage while demo activity is on.
- **Audio:** a show prayer narration ducked music from `0.100` to `0.035` and restored it to `0.100`; the music deck's start time was unchanged (no restart). The server skipped narration while a previous prayer was still speaking, and logs showed the guard working.
- **Browser:** 1080×1920 OBS frame captured, cue card and program line render, prayer wall rotated (Grace/Sarah → Emily/David) with first names only, welcome card rendered with the sample label, no JavaScript errors on the stage or dashboard after reload.
- **Reconnect:** a stage that connects mid-cue receives the current cue, including a welcome, without replaying narration.
- **Theme + pace:** pinning `night` produced `NIGHT PRAYER / Before We Sleep`, then reset to rotate-all; pace persisted and reset to `1`.

**Not tested:** a real TikTok LIVE session (no live channel here), so the actual `MEMBER` welcome was not observed from TikTok — deduplication and greeting text were verified through `show.testWelcome` and engine tests. OBS Studio's own audio routing and multi-hour stability were also not exercised.

## Start on Windows

```bat
bun install
uv venv .venv
uv pip install --python .venv\Scripts\python.exe piper-tts
bun start
```

OBS browser source: **http://localhost:3000/?obs=1** (1080×1920). Dashboard: **http://localhost:3000/admin**. The program begins ~12 seconds after launch once Piper is ready; set `SHOW_ENABLED=false` to start with automation off.

The most useful next step is to observe one real LIVE session so the welcome pacing and the bottom panels can be tuned against actual TikTok join volume.

CHRISTIAN PRAYER LIVE — FULL COPYRIGHT & COMMERCIAL LICENSE AUDIT

Perform a complete copyright and commercial licensing audit of the existing project.

IMPORTANT: Do not redesign or break the existing livestream application. Do not delete or replace existing assets automatically. This task is an audit first, not an asset replacement task.

1. MUSIC COPYRIGHT AUDIT

Scan the entire audio directory and identify every music file.

For each file, determine:

Filename
Track title
Duration
Artist/composer
Original source URL
License type
License URL
Commercial usage permission
Livestream/broadcast permission
TikTok usage permission
Permission to use through OBS or external audio playback
Whether attribution is required
Whether modifications are allowed
Whether the original recording and composition are both licensed

If music is AI-generated, check available generation records and the provider's commercial usage terms.

Do not assume that royalty-free means copyright-free.

Do not assume that a Creative Commons license automatically covers every right needed for a commercial livestream.

2. IMAGE COPYRIGHT AUDIT

Scan all image assets, including:

public/assets/christian/
cathedral backgrounds
church interiors
crosses
candles
Bible images
prayer congregation scenes
generated overlays
any other image directories

For each image, verify:

Original source
Author/photographer
Exact license and version
Commercial use permission
Modification permission
Attribution requirements
Whether cropping to 9:16 is permitted
Whether color grading and image adjustments are permitted
Whether any additional restrictions apply

Check original source pages instead of trusting filenames or existing manifest entries.

3. LICENSE STATUS

Assign one of these statuses:

VERIFIED: Evidence supports commercial use for the intended livestream.

NEEDS_REVIEW: License information is incomplete or broadcast rights are unclear.

REJECTED: License prohibits commercial use or the intended modifications.

UNKNOWN: Source or license cannot be verified.

Never mark an asset VERIFIED without evidence.

4. CREATE A COPYRIGHT AUDIT REPORT

Create:

docs/COPYRIGHT_AUDIT.md

Include:

Every music file
Every image file
Source URLs
Authors
License URLs
Commercial permissions
Attribution requirements
Unresolved questions
Recommended replacements

Also create:

config/copyright-manifest.json

Keep the manifest synchronized with actual local assets.

5. ADMIN DASHBOARD

Add a Copyright & Licensing panel to the existing admin dashboard.

Display:

Total music assets
Total image assets
Verified assets
Needs review
Rejected assets
Unknown assets

Add filters:

Music
Images
Verified
Needs review
Rejected

Each asset should display:

Filename
License
Author
Source link
Commercial usage status
Attribution requirements

Add a button:

SCAN COPYRIGHT & REFRESH REPORT

When clicked:

Scan local audio and image folders.
Compare files against existing manifests.
Identify added, deleted and modified files.
Check available license metadata.
Update the audit report.
Refresh the Admin dashboard.

IMPORTANT: Local file scanning does not prove copyright ownership. Do not automatically classify files without reliable licensing evidence.

6. ATTRIBUTION

Create:

docs/ASSET_ATTRIBUTION.md

Generate copy-ready credits for every image and music asset requiring attribution.

Include author, title, source URL, license URL and modification details.

Keep attribution records even when assets are removed from the active rotation.

7. SAFETY
Do not delete existing music.
Do not delete existing images.
Do not change the live music playlist.
Do not change TTS.
Do not change the congregation system.
Do not change TikTok RPC.
Do not change OBS layout.
Do not interrupt the running server.
8. FINAL REPORT

Provide:

Number of music files audited.
Number of images audited.
Number verified for commercial livestream use.
Number requiring review.
Number rejected.
Assets with missing source information.
Exact attribution requirements.
Screenshots of the new Admin panel.
Any unresolved licensing questions.

Do not claim legal clearance where evidence is insufficient.

(async()=>{

 for(const cat of pages){
  const r=await fetch(`https://mixkit.co/free-stock-music/${cat}/`,{headers:{'User-Agent':'ChristianPrayerLiveAudit/1.0'}});
  const html=await r.text();
  const blocks=[...html.matchAll(/<script[^>]+type="application\/ld\+json"[^>]*>([\s\S]*?)<\/script>/gi)].map(m=>m[1]);
  for(const block of blocks){
   let data; try{data=JSON.parse(block)}catch{continue}
   const walk=(x)=>{if(!x||typeof x!=='object')return; if(Array.isArray(x)){x.forEach(walk);return;} if(x['@type']==='MusicRecording'&&x.url){found.set(x.url,{name:x.name,artist:x.byArtist,genre:x.genre,duration:x.duration,url:x.url,license:x.license,copyrightNotice:x.copyrightNotice,sourcePage:`https://mixkit.co/free-stock-music/${cat}/`});} for(const v of Object.values(x))walk(v);};

 const out=[]; let mismatches=[];

  if(!e){mismatches.push({file:t.file,reason:'not found on catalog page'});continue;}
  const parseDur=s=>{const m=/PT(?:(\d+)M)?(?:(\d+(?:\.\d+)?)S)?/.exec(s||'');return m?(Number(m[1]||0)*60+Number(m[2]||0)):null;};
  if(e.name!==t.title) mismatches.push({file:t.file,reason:`title ${t.title} != ${e.name}`});
  if(e.artist!==t.artist) mismatches.push({file:t.file,reason:`artist ${t.artist} != ${e.artist}`});
  const d=parseDur(e.duration); if(d&&t.durationSeconds&&Math.abs(d-t.durationSeconds)>1) mismatches.push({file:t.file,reason:`duration ${t.durationSeconds} != ${d}`});
  out.push({...e,trackId:t.id,manifestTitle:t.title,manifestArtist:t.artist,manifestDuration:t.durationSeconds});
 }

})();

## Copyright & Commercial Licensing Audit — Complete

I audited every production asset under `public/assets`, the archived music folder, and documentation/reference images. No music or image files were deleted, replaced, or removed from the active playlists.

### Audit results

| Metric | Result |
| --- | ---: |
| Music files audited | **23** |
| — active playlist | **21** (18 enabled) |
| — archived originals | **2** |
| Image files audited | **68** |
| — active Christian broadcast assets | **24** |
| — legacy `public/assets` files | **12** |
| — documentation/reference images | **32** |
| **VERIFIED** | **32** |
| **NEEDS_REVIEW** | **43** |
| **REJECTED** | **0** |
| **UNKNOWN** | **16** |
| Total assets | **91** |

**Music:** All 23 are verified. The active library is 3 project-generated CC0 originals plus 18 Mixkit tracks. Mixkit’s official license permits commercial use and public performance on web/social platforms, including TikTok-style livestreams, but prohibits TV/radio broadcast, CDs/DVDs, video games, remixing, standalone redistribution, and rights registration. Mixkit does not require attribution.

**Images:** 9 of the 24 active images are verified (3 generated overlays, 3 public-domain works, 1 CC0 photo, 2 CC BY photos). The other **15 active images are CC BY-SA** and are marked **NEEDS_REVIEW**, not cleared, because 9:16 cropping and color grading may trigger ShareAlike obligations. The 12 legacy temple-era files and 4 upstream demo images are **UNKNOWN** and should not be broadcast.

**Missing source information:** 16 files — the 12 legacy assets and 4 upstream demo images.

**Attribution:** 17 active images require attribution: the 2 CC BY images and 15 CC BY-SA images. Copy-ready credits, including source, license link, author, and modification notes, are in [ASSET_ATTRIBUTION.md](docs/ASSET_ATTRIBUTION.md).

### Evidence checked

- **Wikimedia Commons:** 21/21 active Commons images matched the current API metadata for license, author, and restrictions.
- **Mixkit:** the official license modal was read; 18/18 tracks matched the catalog’s title, artist, and duration metadata.
- **Original music:** [generate_music.py](scripts/generate_music.py) confirms synthesis from scratch with no samples.
- **Local files:** every manifest entry exists and was SHA-256 hashed. Nothing is missing.
- Raw evidence: [commons-license-evidence.json](docs/commons-license-evidence.json) and [mixkit-license-evidence.json](docs/mixkit-license-evidence.json).

### Admin panel

The new **Copyright & Licensing** panel is at `http://localhost:3000/admin`, above the JSON-RPC console. The **SCAN COPYRIGHT & REFRESH REPORT** button is at the top of that panel.

![Copyright & Licensing admin panel](docs/screenshots/admin-copyright-audit.png)

The panel includes music/image/status filters, search, source links, license status, author, commercial/TikTok permissions, and attribution requirements. It currently renders all 91 audited assets.

### Reports and files

Created:

- [COPYRIGHT_AUDIT.md](docs/COPYRIGHT_AUDIT.md) — full inventory, evidence, permissions, unresolved questions, and recommended replacements.
- [ASSET_ATTRIBUTION.md](docs/ASSET_ATTRIBUTION.md) — copy-ready credits.
- [copyright-manifest.json](config/copyright-manifest.json) — synchronized machine-readable manifest.
- [copyright-audit.js](lib/copyright-audit.js) — fixed-directory scanner with atomic writes, backup, hashing, and report generation.
- [copyright-audit.json](public/copyright-audit.json) — dashboard-readable mirror.
- [copyright-manifest.backup.json](config/copyright-manifest.backup.json)
- Evidence JSON files and the panel screenshot.

Modified:

- [server.js](server.js) — `copyright.get`, `copyright.scan`, `/api/copyright`, and state summary.
- [admin.html](public/admin.html), [admin.js](public/js/admin.js), [admin.css](public/css/admin.css) — panel, filters, scan control.
- [README.md](README.md) — audit documentation and API entries.

### Tests run

- `node --check` on the server, admin script, and audit module — passed.
- Scanner add/remove/modify test: 92 assets after adding a test file, 91 after deletion, and one `changed` hash — passed.
- Panel rendering: 91 assets; `Images + Needs review` filter returned 43 — passed.
- Browser console after a clean reload: no JavaScript errors.
- Existing smoke suite: **129/129 checks passed**.
- No real TikTok LIVE session or legal review was used in this audit.

### Important unresolved issues

1. **CC BY-SA ShareAlike scope** for the 15 cropped/graded images needs legal review.
2. **Mixkit’s TV/radio exclusion** must be checked against every distribution channel, along with its composition/master chain-of-title.
3. **Model, property, and publicity releases** are not covered by copyright licenses, especially for congregation photographs.
4. **Legacy and upstream demo images** have no provenance and must not be broadcast.
5. **Project authorship** for the CC0-generated tracks and overlays should be attested by the owner.

### One runtime limitation

I did not interrupt the running livestream server, as instructed. The new `copyright.scan` RPC and `/api/copyright` route are in [server.js](server.js), but the current process predates them. The panel works now from the static mirror, and the scan button correctly reports that a restart is required. After the next normal restart (`Ctrl+C`, then `bun start`), the button will scan and refresh the reports and dashboard automatically.

The full evidence report is [COPYRIGHT_AUDIT.md](docs/COPYRIGHT_AUDIT.md). This audit is a licensing inventory, not legal clearance.

The most important next decision is whether to keep the 15 CC BY-SA cathedral images under ShareAlike or replace them with CC0/CC BY alternatives.

## Automatic background rotation","newString":"The script rejects licenses outside its allowlist, deduplicates by file hash and writes the manifest.

### Adding images: SCAN IMAGE FOLDER

Drop new `.jpg`, `.jpeg`, `.png` or `.webp` files into any of the seven category folders (subfolders are scanned too), then press **SCAN IMAGE FOLDER** in the *Christian Image Library* panel of the dashboard. There is no restart and no server reload: the asset manifest and copyright audit are rewritten, the background catalog refreshes, and every open OBS/admin client receives the new list over the existing WebSocket.

- A filename starting with **`AI_`** (case-insensitive) is registered as an AI-generated original: `AI_GENERATED`, **VERIFIED**, commercial/social use allowed, no attribution required. This rule is never applied to another filename, and the scanner does not search the internet.
- Any other new file is registered as **NEEDS_REVIEW** with license `Unknown`; Copyright Safe Mode keeps it off the stage until its source and license are recorded in the manifest.
- Existing entries keep their title, source, license and attribution. Only dimensions, file size and hash are refreshed. A renamed file is matched by content hash and keeps its licensing record.
- Deleted files are removed from the catalog but never deleted from disk; the previous manifest is kept as `asset-manifest.backup.json`, plus a timestamped copy in `docs/backups/image-manifests/` when entries are removed.
- Hidden files, thumbnails (`thumb*`, `*-thumb*`), temporary files, unsupported extensions and unreadable/corrupted images are ignored and reported as scan errors.
- Only the seven fixed folders under `public/assets/christian/` are scanned; browser requests cannot supply a path, and the music manifest is never touched.

The OBS stage keeps showing the current background if its file still exists. If it was deleted, the catalog falls back to another broadcast-eligible image automatically.

The image library scanner is implemented, wired into the live catalog, and verified end to end on an isolated instance. Production on port 3000 (PID 43432) was never restarted or interrupted.

## What was added

**Auto-scan of the seven existing folders** — `backgrounds`, `bible`, `candles`, `cathedral`, `church`, `cross`, `jesus` are walked recursively for `.jpg/.jpeg/.png/.webp`. Hidden files, `thumb*/‑thumb`, temporary files, unsupported extensions and unreadable images are skipped and reported as scan errors.

**`AI_` registration rule** — a filename starting with `AI_` (case-insensitive) is registered as `AI_GENERATED` with source/author “AI Generated”, Verified commercial + social + livestream + TikTok + OBS permissions and no attribution. Nothing is inferred for any other filename: new non-AI files are registered as `NEEDS_REVIEW` with license `Unknown`. No network lookups are performed.

**Manifest synchronization** — stable IDs, preserved title/source/license/attribution for already-registered files, technical fields (dimensions, size, SHA-256) refreshed, duplicate entries prevented, deletions removed from the catalog without touching the files, and renames detected by content hash so licensing survives. Writes are atomic, with `asset-manifest.backup.json` before every write and a timestamped copy in `docs/backups/image-manifests/` whenever an entry is removed. The music manifest is never modified.

**Instant catalog refresh** — after a scan the copyright audit re-runs, the background catalog is rebuilt in memory, the current background is kept if its file still exists (otherwise a broadcast-eligible fallback is selected), rotation is reconfigured, and clients receive `images.updated` over the existing WebSocket. No server restart, no page reload.

**Dashboard panel** — *Christian Image Library* with `SCAN IMAGE FOLDER`, totals, per-category counts with AI counts, last-scan time, scan progress/results, and a clickable thumbnail grid that marks AI assets and blocked images.

## Files

**Created:** [lib/image-library.js](lib/image-library.js), [data/image-library-state.json](data/image-library-state.json).

**Modified:** [server.js](server.js), [lib/copyright-audit.js](lib/copyright-audit.js), [public/admin.html](public/admin.html), [public/css/admin.css](public/css/admin.css), [public/js/admin.js](public/js/admin.js), [README.md](README.md), [asset-manifest.json](public/assets/christian/asset-manifest.json), [copyright-manifest.json](config/copyright-manifest.json) (+ backup), [copyright-audit.json](public/copyright-audit.json), [COPYRIGHT_AUDIT.md](docs/COPYRIGHT_AUDIT.md), [ASSET_ATTRIBUTION.md](docs/ASSET_ATTRIBUTION.md).

## Current library (after the final clean scan)

| Category | Images | AI-generated |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Backgrounds | 5 | 2 |
| Bible | 4 | 2 |
| Candles | 6 | 2 |
| Cathedral | 4 | 2 |
| Church | 4 | 0 |
| Cross | 6 | 2 |
| Jesus | 2 | 0 |
| **Total** | **31** | **10** |

**Licensed / broadcast-eligible: 16. Requiring review: 15** (the CC BY-SA photographs already flagged by the audit; AI images are all Verified). The first scan also registered 10 pre-existing `AI_`-prefixed images that were on disk but absent from the manifest.

## Tests actually run

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Existing smoke suite | **166/166 passed** |
| Reliability/schedule suite | **77/77 passed** |
| `AI_test_church.jpg` added → scan | Registered `AI_GENERATED`, status `VERIFIED`, `attributionRequired: false`, appears in `/api/backgrounds`, selectable via `stage.setBackground`, and chosen by `stage.nextBackground` (sequential rotation into it) |
| Non-AI `local_test_no_license.jpg` | Registered `NEEDS_REVIEW`, blocked by Copyright Safe Mode with the reason logged |
| Delete test images → scan | Both removed from manifest and catalog; current background fell back automatically; unrelated records and music manifest unchanged (SHA-1 check) |
| Rename a registered image → scan | Reported as a rename, id/title/license/generatedAt preserved, 0 added / 0 removed |
| Duplicate copy while original exists | Registered as a new file, not a false rename |
| Nested folder, thumbnail, hidden and corrupt files | Nested AI image registered; thumbnail/hidden ignored; corrupt file skipped with an error and not registered |
| Dashboard at 1440×1000 | Panel rendered 31 cards, category counts, status line; scan button completed with “31 images, 10 AI-generated, 0 added…” and refreshed the background grid |
| WebSocket refresh | A scan triggered by curl while the dashboard was open updated it from 31 → 32 cards without interaction |
| Console | No console messages or errors during load and scan |

## Notes and limitations

- **Restart required** to load the new server code. Until then the running production process rejects `images.scan`, and the panel shows a clear “restart to load” message.
- The screenshot could not be captured: the browser tool reported the page “has not been drawn yet” because the app window is minimized/covered. The panel was verified through the DOM, the RPC responses and the WebSocket update instead.
- `data/prayer-state.json` was shared with the isolated test instance; its `settings` were restored to the pre-test snapshot afterwards. Test servers on 3120/3121 are stopped.
- A corrupted *already-registered* file stays in the manifest (dimensions retained) but drops out of the stage catalog, so it cannot appear broken on air.
- Rename detection needs a stored SHA-256; every entry now has one, so renames are detected from the next scan onward.

The most useful next step is to give the 15 review-required images a proper licence editor in the dashboard so they can be cleared without hand-editing JSON.

The handoff document is written: [docs/summary.md](docs/summary.md) — 746 lines, ~7,200 words, 14 major sections plus three appendices. I built it from the actual source, configs, manifests and runtime probes, then did a review pass that corrected five claims I had initially stated too generously.

**What it documents**

- **Overview & architecture** — what the app does, its Buddhist-origin conversion, the single-process Express + `ws` + JSON-RPC design, and an ASCII data-flow diagram.
- **Stack** — verified versions on this machine (Bun 1.4.4, Node 20.18.3, Python 3.12.2, Express 4.22.3, ws 8.22.0, `tiktok-live-connector` 2.5.0), npm scripts, browser APIs in use.
- **Structure** — annotated directory tree with line counts and the role of every module, plus how modules interact.
- **Feature status** — every feature marked ✅ / 🟡 / ⛔ / ❓ across 10 areas (TikTok, Piper, music, stage, program, schedule, reliability, copyright, admin).
- **Data & APIs** — no database (JSON files with their exact schemas), all HTTP routes, 94 RPC methods grouped, 27 WebSocket notifications, request/response envelopes, and the business rules that matter (copyright gate, image registration, schedule application, quiz, congregation, silence detection).
- **Configuration** — environment variable names only, no values; config files; external services (none paid); Windows setup commands.
- **History & decisions** — git timeline, 12 architectural decisions with rationale, coding conventions, and 14 concrete gaps.
- **Status, files, instructions** — uncommitted working-tree inventory, blockers, prioritized next steps, 17 must-read files, and rules for the next model (what not to touch, how to verify, warnings).

**Corrections made during the accuracy review**

- `data/prayer-state.json` uses a 1 s debounced plain write, **not** atomic — only manifests, schedule and health state are atomic.
- `data/merit-state.json` is never loaded; the code only logs that it exists.
- Quiz reveal window clamps to 10–90 s (not 20–90).
- Reconnect disposes the old socket but has **no** timestamp-based stale-event filter — I removed the stronger claim.
- `server.js` section numbers repeat (`10`, `10b`, `10c`), so the file map now reflects the actual labels.

**Limits stated in the document:** no test suites were re-run (both mutate a live server's state and nothing was listening on port 3000 at analysis time), real TikTok gift/comment behaviour is marked unverified, and 15 CC BY-SA images remain legally unresolved.

The document also records the biggest actionable gap: the admin dashboard, `/rpc`, `/api/*` and `/ws` have no authentication and bind to all interfaces.

Securing that surface is the highest-value change before the project is exposed beyond this machine.

Done — one button in `/admin`, one RPC method, one notification, and the stage does all the rendering and speaking.

## What was added

**Admin → TikTok Live Connection → End Session** panel now has a single button, **End Live · Say Goodbye**, with a status line ("Idle" / "Farewell playing on the Live Stage (45s)" / "Farewell finished — end LIVE in TikTok when ready"). The button disables itself while a farewell is on screen, so a double click cannot queue a second reading. It never calls `live.disconnect`, never stops the server, and never touches the programme, rotation or manual background selection.

**New RPC:** `show.farewell`. It broadcasts `show.farewell` to the stage first (visual never waits on speech), then synthesizes the blessing through the existing Piper manager and pushes it on the normal `tts.play` channel with `source: 'farewell'`. The stage's existing audio engine plays it, ducks music automatically, and restores it afterwards. The cue carries all five paragraphs and `displayMs`, so both the screen and the reading come from the server.

**New notification:** `show.farewell`, with `state: 'started' | 'speaking' | 'visual-only' | 'ended'`, `durationMs`, `paragraphs` and `error`. A reconnect replays nothing extra; the server clears the screen window itself.

**Stage:** a full-frame *Until We Meet Again* card (gold cross, "FINAL BLESSING", the four paragraphs, the closing in gold italic, tagline) sits above every other overlay. While it is up, programme cues, the quiz and prayer invitations are suppressed locally — server scheduling is untouched — and it fades out only after Piper has finished, never mid-sentence.

## Tests actually run

Against an isolated instance on port 3120 (live `data/prayer-state.json` backed up first):

- `node --check` on `server.js`, `live.js`, `admin.js`, `audio.js` — all OK.
- Farewell suite: **24/24** — RPC returned `ok: true` in 11 ms, title `Until We Meet Again`, all five sentences present (418 chars), five paragraphs delivered, screen time 45 s, narration `20.05 s · en_US-amy-medium`, duplicate click refused with "A farewell is already playing on the Live Stage.", two `show.farewell` events (`started` → `speaking`) plus `tts.play`.
- Unchanged side effects verified in the same run: background unchanged, TikTok still `connected=true @tinytails99`, show still enabled and on the `afternoon` programme, music volume 0.11, `stage.setBackground` still works, farewell recorded in show history.
- Existing suites: **smoke 168/168**, **reliability 77/77**.
- Real browser check of the actual stage page: clicking the admin button produced the card with 4 paragraphs + closing line, `ttsPlaying: true`, music gain ducked `0.10 → 0.035`; after narration the screen hid itself, `ttsPlaying: false`, music gain back to `0.10` and still playing. Console showed no errors on either page.

## Limitations

- Audio only reaches OBS once the stage's audio is unlocked (the existing "Enable Audio" interaction); a browser that blocks autoplay shows the card silently. That is the pre-existing narration behaviour, not something this feature changes.
- The server must be restarted to load the new code; nothing was listening on port 3000, so no live broadcast was interrupted. The test instance used the configured account and was stopped afterwards.
- The screenshot is the 9:16 stage scaled into the preview browser; OBS itself was not attached.

Add a selectable Farewell Message Library directly below the existing End Live · Say Goodbye button in /admin.

The operator must be able to select a farewell message and play it on the Live Stage (/). The selected message must appear visually on the stage and be narrated using the existing Piper TTS system.

1. Admin UI

In public/admin.html, under the existing End Live · Say Goodbye button:

Message title.
